And therefore, if tomorrow -- if the time between now and tomorrow makes a difference for my learned counsel, I do not want to make a problem for them but we will seek cross-examination either Monday or Wednesday as it suits the schedule. On Beatovic, I have spoken with Mr. Jovanovic and indicated that we would probably seek to exclude based on the Foca ruling, on the Kunarac ruling. There may be some room to discuss certain aspects of it, and if they would like to talk about possibly limiting what might go in, I would be very happy to do so. But I think that if the Chamber reads the ruling, much of it was deemed irrelevant, and I don't know that it would be of much use. But I would be very happy to continue the discussion which we started earlier this week. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am a little confused now. Ms. Susan Somers, if I understood you correctly, you are saying that you would like to continue the discussion with regard to the reports tomorrow? Was that it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: No. Just so the Chamber knows, our position was a firm request, the right under the rule to seek cross-examination for objections as to both, but clearly, on van den Bussche, we will want to cross-examine. On Beatovic, because of the recent Foca case ruling, the Kunarac ruling, there may be some room for agreement about part of it going in without potential objection, but of course we would have to discuss exclusion of another part, so I would like to be able to discuss it with counsel, just to let the Chamber know we have been discussing it. If perhaps by tomorrow we could make some type of announcement to the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I have in my own mind, what I remember, is that the Prosecutor objected to accepting the report without a cross-examination because, with respect to Mr. Van den Bussche, he stepped out of the standards, professional standards, if I can use that term. I think that that was it. Whereas with regard to Mr. Beatovic, the question was irrelevant for the case. So with respect to the other expert, you very cordially followed the request of the Chamber with respect to handing in a written view, written -- is that right, Ms. Somers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: It is, thank you, Your Honour. With respect to Kecmanovic, we are preparing and will have filed next week the written paper by our own expert in refutation of the points raised by Kecmanovic; that is correct. It was the other two who were still left subject to live cross-examination and I will try very hard -- certainly on van den Bussche, we do ask for the live, and if there is some accommodation we can reach on Beatovic, given the recent ruling, I would like to try to work that out with my colleagues if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I understand. Mr. Fila? The question is that we have already prepared the ruling and I can give you the ruling now but I will wait nonetheless. But go ahead, Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The essential difference between me and Ms. Somers - not the misunderstanding but the difference - is that the Kunarac decision in the Kunarac case was a precedent. That was the first time the decision was taken that this was the international and so on. And we agree on that wholeheartedly. The difference lies in the following. In the application of the rule -- provisions of the statute, where it says that the practice of the former Yugoslavia would be taken into consideration, I cannot get an expert witness who is going to speak about rape as an international act and crime, because that is -- it is a crime of that type for the first time, and there are no experts like that. There are just experts in local law, whether it be the United States, your own Portugues law or my own Serbian law, but it just exists for local -- in a local character, and that is the only difference because I think that he is there to speak about the local situation. In other words, we see it locally whereas Ms. Somers considers that this is irrelevant because it is -- that is a local question whereas this present question is an international one. And so that is the crux of the problem, the part of the problem which requires a ruling, and I'm not interested in rape as an international crime in international terms. I'm interested in rape as a local phenomenon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Anyway, it is Women's Day, International Women's Day, and all the other days are men's days. I just wish to seize this opportunity to congratulate all the women working here with us -- and I think that I speak on behalf of all the men here present. So we reconvene tomorrow morning at 9.20 as usual, and my homages to the women and shall we end on that note?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: 3.05 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday the 9th day of March, 2001, at 9.20 a.m. 24 25
